description: A hand crank turns a small pinion, which turns a big gear and rope drum that lifts a crate; no crane arm, motor or people shown

facts.intro: Introduce a recognizable hand winch: a red crank on a small steel gear, a big brass gear on the same axle as an orange rope drum, and a wooden crate hanging from a rope. Everything is still, with the crate low.
facts.cutaway: Inside are the small steel pinion, the big brass gear that its teeth mesh with, and the rope drum on the same axle as that big gear.
facts.drive: A push turns the crank and the small pinion. Its teeth drive the big gear, the drum turns with it, and the rope winds up so the crate climbs.
facts.response: The crank keeps turning. The big gear has more than twice as many teeth, so the drum turns slowly while the crank turns fast, which gives a strong lift.
facts.hold: No part moves for this explanation. The pinion has ten teeth and the big gear twenty-six, so one crank turn moves the drum a little more than a third of a turn.
facts.repeat: A second push turns the crank again. The drum winds in more rope and the crate rises higher, by the same small amount for every crank turn.
facts.limit: The crank turns backwards for a moment. The drum unwinds, the rope pays out and the crate sinks, because nothing else holds the drum.
facts.payoff: Crank, pinion, big gear, drum and rope work together: many easy turns of the crank become a strong, slow lift of a heavy crate. No crane arm or motor is shown.
